problems.problem: The reading ends on 'the gods drink him digit by digit': 'digit' is the lunar term for a kalā, but the sentence never mentions the moon, so a reader has an image without its point and the waxing and waning behind 'the fortnights' is left implicit.
problems.fix: Keep Sāyaṇa's words (ekaikaparṇavṛddhihrāsa; devāḥ kalāḥ pibanti) in plain English, e.g. '...reads the Two as the waxing and waning fortnights, in which Soma the creeper gains and loses a leaf a day and the gods drink his portions one by one.' and hold the 45-word cap.

problems.problem: The reading makes 'the dressed' mean 'those carrying the sacrifice through', but Sāyaṇa glosses śṛtāsaḥ as paripakvāḥ (ripened, i.e. by the observances just named) and gives 'carrying the sacrifice' (yāgaṃ nirvahantaḥ) for vahantaḥ, the key's 'which bear'; the two glosses are merged into one.
problems.fix: '...reads the raw as one whose body no milk vow or like observance has heated, and the dressed who bear as those so ripened who carry the sacrifice through.' (within 45 words).

problems.problem: Spread: Yāska treats this very verse. Sāyaṇa's own commentary on 10.71.5 ends by sending the reader to Nirukta 1.20 (‘अप्येकं वाक्सख्ये स्थिरपीतम्’ (निरु. १.२०) इत्यादि निरुक्तमत्रानुसंधेयम्), and his gloss 'the meaning of speech is flower and fruit' is Yāska's there; the packet's Sarup list missed it (its OCR loses entries), so the one day in the batch where the second roster commentator has a real comment on the key verse went to Sāyaṇa by default (the gate warns Sāyaṇa holds 30 of 30).
problems.fix: Open Sarup's Nirukta 1.20 (archive.org nighantuniruktao00yask, via webfetch with the exact url), take Yāska's words on 'aphalām apuṣpām' verbatim as evidence, and name Yāska, Nirukta 1.20 for the reading (or both, in the two-commentator form, if Sāyaṇa's 'mere reciter' differs from Yāska's); if the page cannot be opened, keep the Sāyaṇa entry as it stands.

problems.problem: 'the world of all three times' renders kālatraya literally and is opaque in English at six in the morning.
problems.fix: '...reads the world, past, present and to come, as his greatness, not his true nature...' and trim elsewhere to stay within 45 words (e.g. 'the quarter as marking the world small beside Brahman, which has no measure' is already tight; drop 'all').

problems.problem: Grammar: the clause before the semicolon is a participial phrase with no subject ('Opening a three-verse hymn ... ;'), so it dangles onto 'Sāyaṇa' and reads as if Sāyaṇa opens the hymn; the reading's closing participle 'contemplating what was to be made' also has no subject. Rule 1 wants a plain sense clause, then the reading.
problems.fix: 'The verse opens a three-verse hymn of origins that ends with the Creator forming sun, moon, heaven and earth; Sāyaṇa, on 10.190.1, takes ‘Law’ as true intention and ‘Truth’ as true speech, born of the fervour spent before creation, which he explains as contemplating what was to be made.' then trim to 45 words (e.g. drop 'three-verse' or 'of origins').

problems.problem: Source lines are inconsistent across the batch: some give the Wikisource page title (ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ९.६६), others '(the printed edition is not named)', and days 123 to 126 use a different form ('Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda ..., sa.wikisource (printed edition not named)').
problems.fix: Use one form for every src, e.g. 'Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda m.h.v, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं m.h (the printed edition is not named), revision N (year)', within 160 characters.
